body.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{prof}}\), construct \(I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}\) and prove \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P\{\theta_P\in I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}\}\ge1-\alpha\] for every strength sequence. On each critical component of \(\mathfrak R\) whose value is evaluated by \(\mathcal V_\alpha\), prove \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}E_P|I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}|-L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\longrightarrow0.\] On \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{recovered}}\), prove the lower comparison \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\gtrsim r_n\). Only on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\), prove \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}E_P|I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}|\asymp L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\asymp r_n.\] The upper comparison must keep the local stochastic contribution \(\rho_n/\kappa_n+1/(n\kappa_n^3)\) separate from the remainders \(\zeta_n\), \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cont},n}\), \(|\mathcal G_c|\exp[-C_{\mathrm{sep}}n\kappa_n^2h_n/4]\), \(2\delta_n\), and twice the maximal probability of each fallback branch in \(\text{def:worked-four-cell-grid}\); the last four expected-length remainders must be \(o(r_n)\), and \(\zeta_n=o(1)\). No upper rate or critical constant is claimed from \(\mathsf{CR}(s,\kappa_\bullet)\), from population separation, or from marginal profiling alone.
body.justification: A single total interval is needed to turn the limit experiment and lower constructions into uniform frequentist inference.
body.gap: Andrews and Mikusheva (2016) condition out a functional nuisance in Gaussian-process moment models. Feir, Lemieux, and Marmer (2016) and Noack and Rothe (2024) use weak-identification-robust residual-jump inversion at a known cutoff. None supplies a certified four-cell profile or its all-strength minimax length under an unknown cutoff.
body.consumer: The interval gives a frequentist benchmark for unknown or administratively uncertain eligibility thresholds, including the binary HIV-retention application studied by Kowalska, van de Wiel, and van der Pas.
